breedtools: design, analysis and 'Breedbase' storage of plant breeding trials

Source: R/breedtools-package.R
breedtools-package.Rd

breedtools designs and analyses plant breeding field trials, from early generations with a single plot per entry to fully replicated trials, and saves the designs into a 'Breedbase' database. The tutorial, vignette("breedtools"), walks through every design and analysis.

Which design?

Start with design_options() when the number of entries is known but the field dimensions, checks or replication are still to be decided.

  • One plot per entry, one location: augmented row-column design with replicated checks.

  • One plot per entry per location, several locations: augmented partially replicated (p-rep) design, without checks.

  • Every entry in every replicate: resolvable (spatial) row-column design.

Augmented row-column designs

Unreplicated entries plus replicated checks in rows, columns and blocks (Federer, Nair and Raghavarao, 1975; Piepho and Williams, 2016), with equal or unequal row and column groups, complete or incomplete blocks of checks, and Latin or D-optimal check placement that keeps checks apart.

  • Plan: augmented_row_column_layouts(), augmented_row_column_capacity()

  • Design: augmented_row_column_design()

  • Map: plot_augmented_row_column_design()

  • Analysis (fixed, random blocks, random entries, SpATS spatial): analyze_augmented_row_column_design()

Augmented p-rep designs

Multi-location trials in which a share of the entries is repeated at each location (Williams, Piepho and Whitaker, 2011), built by search or from alpha and alpha(2) arrays.

  • Plan: augmented_prep_parameters()

  • Design: augmented_prep_design(), augmented_prep_concurrence()

  • Map: plot_augmented_prep_design()

  • Analysis (with replicates and fixed or random genotype x location): analyze_augmented_prep_design()

  • Two-stage weighted analysis with block or SpATS spatial stage 1: analyze_augmented_prep_two_stage()

Resolvable row-column designs

Fully replicated designs optimized for row-column and spatial (linear variance) efficiency, with latinized options (Williams, John and Whitaker, 2006).

  • Design: resolvable_row_column_design()

  • Efficiency, neighbours, AR criterion: resolvable_row_column_efficiency()

  • Map: plot_resolvable_row_column_design()

  • Analysis (RC, LV + RC and AR + RC by REML): analyze_resolvable_row_column()

Saving to Breedbase

Designs are saved as trials with their plots into a breeding program and folder through BrAPI, after checking every name; after harvest, the phenotypic data are saved to the same plots.

  • Log in: breedbase_login()

  • Look up names: breedbase_programs(), breedbase_folders(), breedbase_locations()

  • Check location and accessions before designing: breedbase_check()

  • Convert designs generated with agricolae: as_breedbase_design()

  • Prepare an agricolae trial with its name, location and program: prepare_breedbase_trial()

  • Save (with a dry run first): save_breedbase()

  • Phenotypes: phenotype_template() (sheet with the plot names), save_breedbase_phenotypes() (values by plot and trait name)

  • Analysis results: first_stage_values() and save_breedbase_first_stage() (plot values as a trait of the field plots, trait made by breedbase_adjusted_trait()); second_stage_values() and save_breedbase_analysis() (genotype values as a Breedbase analysis)

Multi-environment trials from Breedbase

  • Read files: read_breedbase_file(), prepare_breedbase_pheno()

  • Error variances (Hartley's Fmax): run_breedbase_variance_check(), hartley_fmax_test()

  • Environment groups (Lin, 1982): run_environment_stratification(), lin_group_environments()

  • Maps: read_locations(), map_environment_groups()

Trait data and two-stage analysis

  • Look: plot_trait(); outliers: find_outliers(), remove_outliers()

  • Two-stage analysis for any design: analyze_two_stage(); single stage: analyze_single_stage()

  • Phenotypes of trials from Breedbase: breedbase_phenotypes()

  • Raw versus first-stage values: compare_first_stage()

Checks

check_setup(), check_design(), check_result(), check_summary(), prediction_accuracy().
